- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After sharp price spikes, model tends to overshoot and then gradually correct — but often undercorrects or lags in the final 5–10 days.
- Mean reversion is not captured well; model fails to anticipate sharp downward corrections after upward moves.
- Forecast tends to be smoother than actual volatility — underestimates volatility spikes and overestimates calm periods.
- Model often fails to adjust downward when true price drops sharply after a peak — exhibits lag in correction.
- In cases with strong upward momentum, model overreacts to recent highs and fails to recognize structural support or reversal signals.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts show persistent bias toward higher prices, especially when recent history includes high volatility or spikes.
